- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.17) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecasted peaks by 3–5%.
- If model shows early sharp downward spikes (e.g., 65–63) following positive sentiment, it often underestimates subsequent rebound; adjust downward bias by +2–4% in next 5–7 days.
- After a strong upward spike (e.g., >75), model frequently overcorrects and forecasts a sharp drop; cap forecasted decline to 10–15% below peak, then allow gradual reversion.
- If sentiment is negative (≤-0.28) and model forecasts a drop, it often fails to capture a subsequent rebound; add 1–3% upward bias in next 3–5 days if sentiment turns neutral or positive.
- Model underestimates long-term trend (30d) when sentiment is volatile or mixed; increase forecasted mean by 1–2% if sentiment average >0.05 over last 7 days.
- If model forecasts a 30d price >75, and sentiment is weak or negative, reduce forecast by 5–8% to avoid overestimating “sustainability” of high prices.
- Model often underestimates late-period (last 7–10 days) price movements when sentiment is positive; add 1–3% upward adjustment to final 5–7 days if sentiment >0.15.
